knowledge:
- key_parameters: Output_Folder=Directory where all generated CSV and PDF results are saved ;; finalCounts=Matrix of raw read counts per transcript (rows are RefSeq NM/NR IDs, columns are samples) ;; sampleMeta=Metadata table associating sample IDs with test conditions and nicknames ;; COLORS=Vector of colors used for plotting (e.g., blue, black, gold) ;; MAX_Genes_for_Heatmap=Maximum number of genes to display on the final differential expression heatmap ;; MAX_GOs_for_Heatmap=Maximum number of GO Terms to display on the projection HMA file ;; MaxGenesInSet=Maximum size of evaluated GO Terms (smaller values speed up projection significance calculation) ;; LIMIT$LFC=Log2 minimum fold-change required for significance ;; LIMIT$HARD=Logical; if TRUE, strictly respects p-value limits. If FALSE, automatically adjusts thresholds to force plot generation even if no genes are strictly significant ;; renormalize=Logical parameter in GSEPD_INIT (default TRUE); set to FALSE if using a pre-normalized table to prevent double normalization
- alternatives: The documentation mentions initializing GSEPD with a DESeqDataSet object (from HTSeq read counts) instead of a raw counts matrix. For generating count tables, HTSeq, RSEM, or coverageBed are mentioned.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for RNA-Seq transcriptomics data with complex samples and low replicate counts (such as human tissues) where confounding factors cannot be easily controlled statistically.
- pitfalls: R column names cannot have spaces or special characters (like + or .). R may silently convert spaces to periods (e.g., "Sample 1" to "Sample.1"), causing mismatches with the metadata table. Test conditions must not contain spaces, as they become column headers and will cause errors. If a condition name contains the letter "x", the delimiter must be changed (e.g., G$C2T_Delimiter <- 'z') to avoid parsing errors. Calculating projection significance for very large gene sets can be slow (controlled by MaxGenesInSet).

workflows.name: gsepd_analysis_pipeline
workflows.intent: Run the complete rgsepd pipeline to perform differential expression, GO enrichment, and multidimensional projection display analysis.
input: finalCounts (matrix of RNA-Seq read counts with RefSeq NM/NR transcript IDs as row names and sample IDs as column names)
sampleMeta (data frame/CSV associating sample IDs with conditions and short names)
workflows.stages:
1. Initialize the GSEPD object with counts, metadata, and output folder using GSEPD_INIT.
2. Define the comparison conditions using GSEPD_ChangeConditions.
3. Customize pipeline parameters (e.g., heatmap limits, fold-change thresholds, gene set size limits).
4. Execute the automated pipeline (DESeq2, GOSeq, and projection calculations) using GSEPD_Process.
5. Generate visualizations including gene-specific heatmaps using GSEPD_Heatmap and PCA plots using GSEPD_PCA_Plot.
workflows.code:
isoform_ids <- Name_to_RefSeq(c("GAPDH","HIF1A","EGFR","MYH7","CD33","BRCA2"))
rows_of_interest <- unique( c( isoform_ids ,
                    sample(rownames(IlluminaBodymap),
                    size=5000,replace=FALSE)))
G <- GSEPD_INIT(Output_Folder="OUT",
          finalCounts=round(IlluminaBodymap[rows_of_interest , ]),
          sampleMeta=IlluminaBodymapMeta,
            COLORS=c(blue="#4DA3FF",black="#000000",gold="#FFFF4D"))
G <- GSEPD_ChangeConditions( G, c("A","B"))
  G$MAX_Genes_for_Heatmap <- 30
  G$MAX_GOs_for_Heatmap <- 25
  G$MaxGenesInSet <- 12
  G$LIMIT$LFC <- log( 2.50 , 2 )
  G$LIMIT$HARD <- FALSE
  G <- GSEPD_Process( G )
  print(isoform_ids)
  GSEPD_Heatmap(G,isoform_ids)
  GSEPD_PCA_Plot(G)
